title: Longest Sorted Run of All Five Vowels
statement:
You get a string word made only of the letters a, e, i, o and u.

Find the longest contiguous piece of word that uses all five vowels and whose letters never go backwards in the order a < e < i < o < u. Repeats are fine, so "aaeiioouu" qualifies. Return its length, or 0 if no piece qualifies.

examples.why: "aaeiioou" (8 letters) uses every vowel in order. The run after it, "aeiouu", is only 6.
After "aei" the order drops back to "a", and the run "aaioou" skips e. No run has all five.
The leading "u" cannot start a run that still needs a, so the answer is "aeiou".

constraints: word has only the letters a, e, i, o, u
hints: A qualifying piece cannot cross a spot where the next letter is smaller than the previous one. So the string splits into sorted runs.
Within one sorted run, the whole run is the best candidate: extending it only adds letters. What do you need to know about a run to decide if it qualifies?

Scan once, tracking the current run's start and how many distinct vowels it has (the count goes up whenever the letter changes). Reset when the order drops; record the run length whenever the count is 5.

explain.intuition:
Whenever a letter is smaller than the one before it, no valid piece can contain both, so the string falls apart into maximal sorted runs. A run that starts with e or later contains no a at all, so nothing inside it qualifies. A run that starts with a qualifies as a whole if it contains all five vowels, and no piece of it is longer than the whole. So the answer is the longest sorted run that has all five vowels.

So one pass is enough. Keep the current run's length and the number of distinct vowels in it. Because the run is sorted, a new distinct vowel shows up exactly when the letter changes. When the letter drops, start a new run. Whenever the distinct count reaches 5, the run so far is a candidate.
steps: For i from 1: if word[i] < word[i−1], start a new run: len = 1, kinds = 1.
Otherwise add 1 to len, and if word[i] ≠ word[i−1] add 1 to kinds.
If kinds === 5, set best = max(best, len). A run with 5 kinds that is still sorted must have started at a.
pitfalls: Checking only that all five vowels appear, not that the run started with a. Counting changes handles this: a run starting at e can reach at most 4 kinds.
Forgetting to update best while the run continues. The longest run may end at the last character, with no drop after it.
Comparing letters by vowel index from a lookup table but resetting only on u → a. Any drop, such as o → i, breaks the run.

solutions.title: Extend from every start
solutions.idea: From each start, extend while the letters stay sorted and record the length whenever all five vowels have appeared.

solutions.title: One pass over sorted runs
solutions.idea: Track the current sorted run's length and its number of distinct letters. Reset on a drop.

followups: The alphabet is any ordered set of k letters and the piece must use all of them. What changes?
Count how many qualifying pieces there are, not just the longest. Does the run structure still help?
